Mapping a Recording with the Timestamp Notes

Stamp the sections, tap the bars, loop a verse: Timestamp Notes, and what to do when YouTube won’t play.

The Timestamp Notes turns a recording into a map: where each section starts, where every bar falls, and how fast the band is really playing. With the map you can jump straight to the bridge, loop a verse until you have it, and see whether the drummer speeds up in the last chorus.

Keep the player open in a second tab and work through the steps with a song you know.

1. Load a recording

Open the player. There are three ways in:

  1. A file. Drop a video or audio file (MP3, M4A, WAV, MP4…) on the box that says Drop a video or audio file here, or press Choose file. A file is the best choice: it plays on this page, the timing is exact, and nothing can block it.
  2. A YouTube link. Paste it into the box and press Load (or Return).
  3. A link in the address. timestamp-player.html?v= followed by a YouTube link or id loads it straight away, which is handy for a link on a class page.

The big clock shows where the recording is. Space or Return plays and pauses from anywhere on the page; the arrows (or h / l) go 5 seconds back or on.

If YouTube says the video won’t play here, skip to When YouTube won’t play it.

2. Stamp the sections and the moments

Listen through once. There are two keys, and both put a row in the Timestamps column, in time order:

  • S where a section starts (the next step).
  • C whenever anything else happens: a key change, a fill you want to learn, a wrong note in your own recording.

For a C note:

  1. Press C. A row appears with the time.
  2. The cursor jumps into the row’s note field. Type what happened (“Chorus”, “sax fill”, “key change”).
  3. Leave the note with Esc, or type jk quickly. The letters are taken back out.
  4. Keep listening and stamping.

Click any time in the list to jump there. Untick Jump to the note field after a stamp if you’d rather stamp everything first and write the notes afterwards.

Everything is saved in the browser as you go, so a reload doesn’t lose it. Copy all gives you a plain list (01:23 Chorus) and Paste… reads one back. Saving the whole song is covered in step 7.

3. Name the sections

Press S where a section starts. The row is tinted blue and has a menu: Intro, Head, Verse, Pre-chorus, Chorus, Bridge, Interlude, a solo for each instrument, Shout, Outro, and the form letters (A, then A′ and B, and so on). Other… at the bottom lets you type a label of your own. A new stamp starts with the label of the one before it, so chorus after chorus is just S, S, S.

  • A label used more than once is numbered for you: two Heads become Head 1 and Head 2 everywhere.
  • Under the Timestamps, the page counts how many choruses each soloist takes (in a pop song, how many bars).
  • If you’ve pasted the words (step 6), S stamps their next section instead.

What each label means, and how the counting works: Section Labels.

A C note that names a section also counts as one (older song files work this way):

Write For example
A section word first Intro, Verse 1, Pre-chorus, Chorus 2, Bridge, Solo, Instrumental, Interlude, Break, Outro, Coda, Tag, Vamp, Head, Ending, Turnaround
A letter, with or without a number A, B, A2
Anything after § § horns come in, § modulation

Any other note (“sax fill”, “check this bar”) stays a plain stamp.

Stamp each section on its first downbeat. You don’t have to be exact; the next step fixes that.

4. Tap the bars

Now give the recording its bars.

  1. Set Beats a bar: 4 for most pop and rock, 3 for a waltz, 6 for a slow 6/8 counted in six.
  2. Go back to the start (click the first stamp, or drag the video’s own slider).
  3. Press Return to play, and press B on beat 1 of every bar. Count “1 2 3 4” under your breath and press on each “1”.
  4. Watch the line above the panels. It shows Bar 7 · Chorus and flashes on every tap.

Fixing mistakes:

  • Backspace takes back the last tap.
  • Tapping near a bar you already tapped (within about a sixth of a second) replaces it. So to fix one spot, go back a few bars before it and tap through it again.
  • Open the Bars panel. Any bar much longer or shorter than the others is highlighted yellow: that is almost always a missed or doubled tap. Click its time to jump there and tap it again.
  • Fill from the tempo: tap a stretch (the head), stamp where each later section starts (S), and it puts in the rest of the bars, each solo a whole number of choruses when it’s close. Tap B where a guessed bar drifts. See Section Labels.
  • Fill gaps puts in the bars of a stretch you missed. Halve bars / Double bars fix taps made every half bar or every other bar (Undo puts them back).
  • A bar really in another meter (a bar of 2 before a chorus)? Change its Beats in the Bars panel.
  • In the Sections panel, ⚠ beside two sections next to each other (9 bars then 7, say) means the stamp between them is probably a bar off.

Once the bars are in, every section moves onto the nearest tapped bar, so a stamp a little early or late lands on the right downbeat. The Sections panel now says Verse 1 · bars 9–16.

The summary line tells you the tempo: 64 bars · about 118 bpm (114–122). A narrow range means a steady band (or a click track); a range that climbs through the song means it speeds up.

Tip: listen to the first bars a couple of times before tapping. Tapping goes much better when you already know where “1” is. In a song with a pickup, start tapping at the first full bar.

5. Use the map

  • Jump. Click a section’s time, or a bar’s time in the Bars panel.
  • Loop. Press Loop beside a section, or Shift+L while the playhead is in it. The recording goes back to the start of the section every time it reaches the next one. Press Shift+L again (or the button, now saying Looping) to stop.
  • Phrases. The Phrases panel cuts each section into 2-, 4- or 8-bar phrases, each looped from its lead-in. P loops the phrase under the playhead, , and . step to the one before or after, and T sends it to the Notation page to write down.
  • Without the audio. Once the timings are in, clicking a section (in the chord grid, the menu in Now playing, or the Sections panel) moves to it even with nothing loaded, so you can check and fix the map anywhere.

6. Words, chords and the chord grid

  • Words and chords. Paste a song from Ultimate Guitar (chords above the words, [Verse 1] headings) and press Convert: it becomes ChordPro. No words yet? Sections from stamps puts your section labels in instead, so the chord grid shows each section’s bars anyway.
  • Chord timing. Press N as each chord starts (Shift+N takes the last one back); which chord it is comes from the words. Or play it all in from a MIDI keyboard: connect it in the box at the top of the right sidebar. The left hand plays a note on every barline (two together where a section starts), the right hand the chords.
  • The chord grid follows the section under the playhead. When a section’s chords are in the right places, press Timing is right to show them all.
  • Send on. Notation page (melody) sends the sections and chords for writing down the tune; Backing Track (style) sends the chart to play along with, at the tapped tempo.

7. Save and start again

  • Save song file saves everything in one .json: the stamps, the bars, the words and chords, the chord timing, the phrases and the link. Open file reads one back (older .txt stamp lists and bar-map .json files open too).
  • The browser keeps one song at a time. Before you start on another, save the song file, then press Clear all data. It asks first (press it again within a few seconds), then empties everything kept for the song: stamps, bars, words and chords, chord timing, grids and phrases. The page reloads with nothing loaded. Your page settings (column widths, folded parts, the MIDI keyboard) stay.

When YouTube won’t play it

Some videos show Video unavailable with a message like “…blocked it from display on this website or application”. The player shows the reason and YouTube’s error number in its own words:

Error Means
101 or 150 The owner, or a rights holder such as a music publisher, blocks it from playing here
100 Removed, or private
2 Not a valid video link
153 YouTube couldn’t tell which page asked for it

First, try another browser window. These blocks depend on the browser as well as the website. The same video can play in one browser and be refused in another. Try a private window with extensions off, or another browser. If it plays there, use that.

If it still won’t play, follow along in a YouTube tab. The video plays on YouTube itself, and the player keeps its own clock in step with it.

  1. Press Follow in a tab (next to Load, or on the error message). YouTube opens in a new tab.
  2. Put the two windows side by side, so you can see YouTube and press keys on the player.
  3. In YouTube, pause the video at a time you can read, for example 0:00 or 1:05.
  4. On the player, type that time into Clock to and press Return. The big clock shows it.
  5. Start the video in YouTube, click back onto the player straight away, and press Return as close to the same moment as you can. Or start the clock on a sound you can hear: pause at the start of a bar, set the clock to that time, then press Return here on the first note.
  6. Check it after a few seconds. If the clock is ahead, press [** to pull it back 0.1 s; if it’s behind, press **].
  7. If you slow YouTube down (its settings gear, Playback speed), choose the same Speed on the player.

Now C, B, section names and the bar map work as before.

What can’t work: the player can’t see or steer YouTube’s tab. YouTube’s tab cuts itself off from the page that opened it, so the player can’t pause it, move it, or close it.

  • Jumping (clicking a stamp, section or bar) opens a new YouTube tab at that time, and the clock stops there. Pause the old tab first, or you’ll hear two copies, then close it yourself. Press Return when the new tab starts playing.
  • Looping isn’t available. Loop in YouTube instead (right-click the video and choose Loop) or drag its slider back.
  • The clock drifts a little. Expect to nudge by a tenth of a second or two, and check it again when you jump.

The best fix is a file. If you have the recording (bought, from the band, from your own phone), drop it on the player instead. Everything works, exactly.

Exercise: map a song in 15 minutes

Choose a song you’re learning and do this in one sitting.

  1. Load it (5 min). Play it through once, stamping and naming every section.
  2. Bars (5 min). Set the beats, go back to the start, tap every bar. Fix the yellow bars.
  3. Check (3 min). Click through the sections. Does each one start on a downbeat? Write down the tempo and whether it changes.
  4. Practise (2 min, then as long as you like). Loop the hardest section and play or sing along.
  5. Save the song file.

Questions to answer about your song:

  • How many bars is each section? Are the verses and choruses the same length every time?
  • Is the tempo steady? Where does it change?
  • Is there a bar of 2 or a bar of 6 anywhere? (A bar in the Bars panel whose length is half or one and a half times the others, that you tapped correctly, is one.)

All the keys

Key Does
Return Play and pause (following a tab: start and stop the clock)
Space Play and pause
← →, or h l 5 seconds back / on
S Stamp a section (choose its label)
C Stamp a note
Esc, or jk Leave a note field
B A bar starts here
Backspace Take back the last bar tap
Shift+L Loop the section under the playhead; again to stop
N / Shift+N A chord starts here / take the last one back
P Loop the phrase under the playhead
, / . The phrase before / after
T Send the phrase to the Notation page
[** / **] Following a tab: clock 0.1 s back / on
